title: Copy command leaves a lot of zombie processes
body:
**Basic information**
`Debug log`: [zellij-22.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19166555/zellij-22.log)

`zellij --version`: zellij 0.41.2

`stty size`: 33 140

`uname -av`: 
`Linux user 6.1.0-31-amd64 #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Debian 6.1.128-1 (2025-02-07) x86_64 GNU/Linux`

## Reproduction steps

1. Run zellij session using config with `copy_command` set  and `copy_on_select` enabled 
2. Select some text to make it into clipboard
3. Paste it somewhere to make sure it works
4. Copy again couple times
5. run command `ps ax|grep wl-copy`  and see something like
```
 581867 ?        Z      0:00 [wl-copy] <defunct>
 614145 ?        Z      0:00 [wl-copy] <defunct>
 649179 ?        S      0:00 wl-copy
```
where <defunct> is a zombie.


## Issue description
On every copy on select new child process with copy command is spawned and previous command process (if any) turns into zombie process. My current copy command is `wl-copy`, but had similar issues with `xclip`, so likely it has issues with other copy commands.

participant4
comments.body: The force kill only happens if we try to reap the process and it has not been reaped for more than 1 second. I'm not sure what else you'd expect?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
>  if we try to reap the process 

If it returns `Some(None)` means child didn't finished execution yet. 
if we craft custom script, for example: 

```shell
echo -e  "#!/bin/sh \n sleep 1.5 \n wl-copy" > /tmp/copy_delay.sh && chmod +x /tmp/copy_delay.sh
```
and setup it as our copy command in config:
```
copy_command "/tmp/copy_delay.sh"
```
it will fail to copy because of 1s timeout, though it should work just fine.
if you change sleep time from 1.5 to 0.5 it will work as intended with half second delay, because it will fit the timings. 

though, its a rare case to have copy command work for such a long time, it still a legit possibility - weak hardware/embed, work over some pigeon network etc.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body: While I understand where you're coming from - I think the vast majority of cases in which this command will take more than 1 second are when the user misconfigured it or there's some sort of issue. I'd rather optimize for those cases rather than have the potential for a misconfiguration to cause a thread leak, or to overcomplicate this part of the code by hooking into an async runtime. Thanks for pointing this out though.

comments.body: Got it. Than we can consider zombie apocalypse prevented.
